title: Picture this
topic: Photography and the stories behind images

vocab.name: Photography
words: the position from which you look at or photograph something
Try taking the photo from a low *angle*.
a photo taken very near the subject
This *close-up* shows the details of the flower.
a clear difference between light and dark or colours
Black and white photos often have strong *contrast*.
the feeling of distance in a picture
The trees in front give the photo more *depth*.
Simple images are often the most *effective*.
a bright light on a camera used in the dark
Turn off the *flash* in the museum.
the edges of a picture; to arrange the edges
*Frame* your subject in the centre of the picture.
to make something easy to notice
That photo had a huge *impact* on the public.
to aim something towards a person or thing
*Point* the camera *at* the bird and wait.
to prepare equipment so it's ready to use
It took ten minutes to *set up* the tripod.

a photo, or a part of a film
That's the best *shot* of the whole trip.
the person or thing in a photo
The *subject* of the portrait is her grandmother.
a person who looks at an image or watches something
The photo makes the *viewer* feel sad.

grammar.title: Modals of deduction
grammar.short: must, might, could, can't – present and past

slides.sub: Picture this: the story behind the photo
slides.hook: Look at a famous photo. Where might it have been taken? How must the subject have felt?

rows: might / may / could have + past participle

p: We use these modals to guess about a photo or a situation now, based on the evidence we can see.
ex: She's carrying a tripod. She **must be** a photographer.
The subject is smiling. He **might be** looking at his family.
That **can't be** a real photo – the contrast is impossible!

p: For actions in progress now: modal + be + verb-ing.
ex: They **must be shooting** a close-up – look at the camera angle.
The photographer **could be pointing** the camera at the bird.

p: To guess about the past: modal + have + past participle.
ex: The photographer **must have waited** hours for that shot.
This picture **might have been** taken by chance.
He **can't have used** a flash – the photo is so dark.

slides.title: What happened before the shot?
text: In this black-and-white photo, eleven workers are eating lunch on a steel beam high above New York. They **must have been** very brave – or very used to heights!
Some experts think the shot **might have been** planned by the photographer to promote the new skyscraper. The men **can't have been** completely relaxed, but they look calm.
The viewer **must feel** the impact of the empty space below them. In fact, that is why the photo is so powerful.

items: He mustn't be the photographer – he hasn't got a camera.
He can't be the photographer – he hasn't got a camera.
For negative deduction, use can't, not mustn't.
She must took the shot from a helicopter.
She must have taken the shot from a helicopter.
Past deduction: modal + have + past participle.
The photo could have be edited.
The photo could have been edited.

slides.q: The whole photo is out of focus. The photographer ___ moved the camera.
slides.e: Strong evidence about the past → must have + participle.

slides.q: That ___ the original photo. The original is in a museum in Paris!

p: can't / couldn't = I'm sure it's not true.

grammar.title: Verbs + -ing / to infinitive
grammar.short: enjoy taking, decide to take, remember / stop / try

slides.sub: Picture this: learning to take better photos
slides.hook: Do you enjoy taking photos? What would you like to learn to photograph?

rows: enjoy, like, love, hate, don't mind
I enjoy taking close-ups of flowers.
Avoid using the flash in museums.
slides.note: Also use -ing after prepositions: I'm interested in learning photography.

rows: want, would like, hope, plan, decide
She decided to shoot in black and white.
He refused to delete the photo.
We managed to find the perfect angle.

p: Some verbs can take both forms but the meaning changes.
ex: I **remember taking** this shot by chance. (a memory)
**Remember to set up** the tripod! (don't forget)
She **stopped taking** photos. (she doesn't do it any more)
She **stopped to take** a photo of the sunset. (in order to)
I **tried to keep** the subject in focus, but it moved. (an effort)

slides.title: Five tips for better photos
text: 1. **Avoid using** the flash – natural light is more pleasant.
2. **Try getting** closer to your subject. A close-up can have a big impact.
3. **Don't forget to check** the frame before you shoot.
4. **Keep practising** every day. Many great shots happen by chance!
5. **Remember to look** for things out of the ordinary. The viewer **will enjoy discovering** them.

items: She decided to enter the competition.

slides.q: I can't afford ___ a new lens.
We stopped ___ a photo of the sunset.
slides.e: We stopped in order to take a photo.

p: -ing after enjoy, avoid, finish, keep, mind, suggest and prepositions.
to + verb after want, decide, hope, plan, manage, refuse, promise.
remember / forget / stop / try change meaning.
